common_instruction: Work from the supplied task and evidence packet within its stated scope. Produce the requested practical artifact and rationale. Treat supplied facts as evidence for this decision exercise, not as actions you performed. State missing evidence and unresolved decisions precisely; continue independent work where possible. Use available reference material when useful. Do not invent requirements, tool execution, or results.

cases.name: five concerns, one endpoint
cases.prompt: Propose candidate groups for adding one REST decision-detail endpoint. Current inspection: `app/decision.ts` contains registration, validation, handler and serialization; `api/openapi.yaml` documents it; `app/decision.test.ts` and the generated client are relevant consumers. These are small, same owner, same dependency position, one-session work. The input lists those five concerns separately. Preserve usable endpoint/errors/docs and verification; say why to merge or separate. Planning only, no final scheduling requested.
expectations: One coherent group, or a justified second merge candidate, not five dispatches. Own caller/generated-client consistency and falsifiable endpoint evidence. No fictional path inspection or schedule/plugin requirement.

cases.name: hidden irreversible migration
cases.prompt: The accepted architecture separately deploys an additive schema compatibility change and a large irreversible backfill. Current inspection: `db/schema.sql`, `api/history-reader`, and `worker/history-reader` consume the old representation; `ops/backfill` performs transformation. Old history must remain readable during rollout; accepted transformation/no-loss rules are explicit and not open for redesign. The proposal is one group, “update database.” Return candidate boundaries, preserved obligations, safety/dependencies, surfaces, and who proves real upgrade and both consumers. Do not turn every file into a task.
expectations: Separate routine compatibility from hazardous separately deployed operation; name prerequisites and proof owner, both consumers, rollout invariant. No new migration policy or collapsed safety boundary; ordinary mechanics need no new product approval.

cases.name: natural ownership and merge candidates
cases.prompt: Decompose auth work: hash algorithm replacement and registration strength validation share owner/dependency/files and agreed semantics; login rate limiting is platform-owned across a process boundary with an accepted auth/platform contract; API docs need refreshing. Inspection confirms `auth/register`, `auth/login`, `platform/limiter`, their contract tests, and `docs/auth-api`. Return compact candidates, merge candidates where appropriate, integration/verification ownership, and one accepted registration/login scenario's required groups. Scheduling/assignment is not requested.
expectations: Keep or explicitly merge hash/validation; preserve platform/process seam. Docs may join relevant owner or remain justified candidate, not forced standalone. Shared guarantee and proof ownership visible; no unapproved algorithm/strength/rate policy redesign.

cases.name: product proof without per-seam task explosion
cases.prompt: Decompose the accepted browser configuration → API → worker → persistence → explanation journey, plus quota/defer/resume. Current inspected surfaces are `web/client`, `app/config-api`, `app/decision-api`, `worker/discovery`, `worker/queue`, `db/migrations`, related tests and build config. Each layer has local tests; the client still has a product-owned mock-detail fallback, a known integration risk. Propose coherent groups with obligations, peer prerequisites, and assembled-proof ownership. Explain any early vertical proof; do not create one E2E task per arrow.
expectations: Normal module/capability groups plus eventual real composition proof; mark fallback removal and real endpoint ownership. Early vertical proof justified by missing/fallback seam, not ritual at every boundary. Recovery obligation translates to actual proof; no union-of-unit-suites acceptance.

cases.name: unlocked shared file, stale reads, independent progress
cases.prompt: The host has no file-lock guarantee. Two semantically independent groups will edit separate settings in `config/shared.yaml`; both may read the same old bytes. Their tests also share one temporary database name. A third group changes only isolated docs. Propose coordination and dependencies that keep useful parallelism without lost writes or contaminated evidence. You may choose ordinary isolation, an integrator, or ordered publication; no plugin installation is allowed.
expectations: Explain stale-read/lost-write risk and shared test state; choose concrete re-read/reconcile/integrator or isolated merge arrangement plus isolated/ordered DB tests. Independent docs/analysis can run in parallel. Do not invent locks or globally serialize all work.

cases.name: mutation locks do not protect the read/edit cycle
cases.prompt: The host serializes individual file writes but does not lock the whole read/edit/verify cycle. Group A and B each read the old generated client and later publish changes derived from different API schema revisions. They use the same test port. The API contract is agreed, and a schema revision must be integrated before final client generation. Assess proposed “parallel is automatically safe because writes are locked,” and propose a proportionate corrected arrangement.
expectations: Mutation locking does not prevent stale snapshots, inconsistent generated outputs, or port interference. Assign stable-schema prerequisite and generation/publication responsibility, re-read/reconcile and combined verification, isolated/ordered test resources. Do not forbid all parallel work or change accepted API semantics.

cases.name: honest surface uncertainty and decision ownership
cases.prompt: Planning-only analysis has inspected `api/export` and its caller tests. A background consumer and generated schema are suspected but not inspected. The accepted promise says “export accepted records”; whether “accepted” includes deferred records is unresolved and user-owned. Choose candidate grouping/discovery and identify the exact decision question. Distinguish ordinary serialization/test choices from product semantics. Do not assert guessed paths exist, compile final write scopes, or block unrelated inspection. Later executable handoff will need complete authorized surfaces.
expectations: Label unknown targets unverified and assign discovery; preserve exact decision for owner, continue independent work. No invented deferred-record semantics or needless approval of ordinary mechanics. Planning-only exact scope deferral is legitimate; executable handoff must cover real consumers/tests/generated source once known.
